evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.1.115: somnum capere (Lewis & Short s.v. somnus)
Traupman 38: to take a nap, brevem somnum capere
terms.comment: “Take a short sleep”, at any hour; merīdiāre is the midday nap.

phrases.latin: deinde in cubiculō albō, trānsennā dēmissā, merīdiāvit
phrases.english: then he had a nap in the white bedroom with the shutter down
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 38, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
